title: ÆTHER: Hindustani fusion, evening theme v2 FAST (wordless humming, 150 s, one take)
story: Dusk over a city rooftop: the day's noise fades, the lights come on, and a calm, hopeful evening opens up.

brief.notes: Jithesh 3 Nov 13:47: 'i need a hindustani fusion song.' One take only (his rule). No AI lyrics (he called written lyrics 'really bad'): a soft wordless female humming and aalaap carries the tune instead, which he loves. Complete shape, 2.5 min, with a real build and ending. Raga Yaman in D (evening, serene and romantic). Natural instruments, close and dry, no heavy echo; the processed layer stays light and separate. v2: Jithesh 13:59 on v1: 'its fine but too slow'. Same tune idea and sound, much faster and more energetic: short 6 s opening, groove from 6 s at 118 BPM, faster drut section.

prompt: A complete, original modern Hindustani classical fusion piece, bright, energetic, driving and uplifting, for an evening in the city. Fast and lively from early on, never slow or sleepy. Raga Yaman, a Lydian scale, in D: D E F# G# A B C#. The melody climbs C# E F# G# A, leans on the raised fourth G#, rests on F# and comes down A G# F# E D, in quick, catchy phrases with fast taans (rapid runs) and meend glides, soft andolan shakes on F# and C#. Lead voice: a soft, close, natural wordless female humming and aalaap on open vowels 'aa' and 'mm', no words, no lyrics, no language, carrying the catchy main tune. Natural instruments, all played by real musicians, close and dry, no heavy echo or delay, never chopped: a bamboo bansuri flute, a sitar with fast jhala strumming, a santoor shimmer, tabla playing fast, a tanpura drone on D and A. Modern fusion body underneath: deep punchy bass, a tight kick and crisp snare, handclaps, a light warm synth pad, and a quiet separate electronic layer of chopped, stuttered veena and a reversed swell into each new section. Modal harmony over the D pedal, no Western pop chord loop. Tempo 118 BPM, fast keherwa groove. Shape: 0-6 s a lone bansuri plays a rising 3-note call D F A with the last note bent up over the drone; at 6 s the tabla, bass and kick come in at full tempo; 6-30 s the humming states the catchy main tune over the driving groove; 30-60 s sitar and bansuri trade the tune in quick call and answer, santoor sparkles; 60-90 s the groove gets even faster into drut teentaal, sitar jhala and tabla play a thrilling jugalbandi exchange, each phrase quicker than the last; 90 s one beat of silence, then the biggest final statement of the tune with humming, bansuri, sitar and full groove together; 130 s the tabla and sitar play a fast three-times-repeated tihai and the whole band lands together on one hard hit on D; ends on the bansuri playing D F A.
